- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates downside; add buffer or adjust downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply decay or smoothing to prevent overreaction.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1 to -1), model fails to adjust quickly; introduce lag correction or sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; apply mean-reversion bias toward historical 30-day average if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often drifts toward overoptimistic trend; cap forecast growth to 2–3% per day unless sentiment confirms strong momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after spike, model often fails to anticipate; add early warning buffer for downward correction.
